senses.gloss:
Ujjayinī
(‘the victorious’)
------------------------------------------
Ujjayinī is one of the seven ancient, most holy, cities capable of giving लिबेरतिओन् (mokṣadāyaka). It got this name because शिव is said to have vanquished and killed Tripurāsura here. It was also known by several other names such as Avantī, Kanakaśṛṅga, Kauśasthalī, अमरावती and Viśālā. It has been identi-fied with the modern Ujjain city in Madhya Pradesh, which is 80 kms. (50 miles) to the north of Indore.
It was the capital of the legendary emperor विक्रमादित्य (circa 57 B. C.), in whose court the navaratnas or nine gems of scholars like कालिदास, धन्वन्तरि, अमरसिṁह, वराहमिहिर and वररुचि were believed to have existed.
The city is 486 metres (1620 feet) above the sea-level and is situated on the bank of the Śiprā (or Siprā) river.
It is famous for the महाकाल temple —one of the twelve ज्योतिर्लिङ्गस् (See JYOTIRLIṄGAS.) and as the fourth place where the कुम्भमेला festival is held once in twelve years. It is observed when बृहस्पति or गुरु (the planet जुपितेर्) enters the Siṁharāśi (Leo, the fifth sign of the zodiac) in the month of Vaiśākha (generally in April).
According to the Śivapurāṇa (1.46) महाकाल is शिव who emerged out of the earth and destroyed the demon Dūṣaṇa. At the request of the local devotees he agreed to stay on there itself.
The महाकाल temple has a cellar floor housing the महाकाल-लिङ्ग and a ground floor housing ओङ्कारेश्वर-लिङ्ग.
Devotees wishing to have the दर्शन (seeing) of the deity have to take bath in the Śiprā river at the Rāmghāṭ and proceed to the shrine.
Everyday, at 4:30 a.m. ārati is done to the महाकाल-लिङ्ग by sprinkling the ashes of a freshly cremated corpse of the previous day. This is done on all the days of the year!
Āvantikādevī is the consort of the Lord in this temple complex.
The Harasiddhi temple (of मोथेर् अन्नपूर्णा) is another important shrine. Other temples are those of Gopāla (Rādhā-कृष्ण), Gaḍhakālikā (or Mahākālī), Kāla-भैरव, Maṅgalanātha and चिन्तामणि गणेश.
About 3 kms. (1.8 miles) from the temple of Gopāla is the सान्दीपनि आश्रम, where कृष्ण and बलराम were educated by the sage सान्दीपनि.
Ancient astronomers assigned 0° (zero degree longitude) to उज्जयिनी (like Greenwich) and based their calculations on it. There is an observatory (Vedhaśālā) built by the king Jai Singh (circa A. D. 1700).
